title: Ban Chiang
summary: Ban Chiang is a large prehistoric earthen mound of habitation and burials in Udon Thani Province, northeast Thailand. UNESCO reports continuous occupation from 1495 BC to about 900 BC, with evidence of rice farming, domesticated animals, pottery and bronze tool-making. Penn Museum and Thailand's Fine Arts Department excavated it in 1974-75, and UNESCO inscribed it in 1992.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives 1495 BC to c. 900 BC from C-14 and thermoluminescence dating; Penn Museum gives only "nearly four thousand years ago". Years are astronomical (1495 BC = -1494).

where.modern_name: Ban Chiang Archaeological Site, Nong Han District, Udon Thani Province, Thailand
where.historical_name: Prehistoric settlement and burial mound in the Mekong River watershed, northeast Thailand (no state at this date in the sources)

importance.justification: UNESCO calls it the most important prehistoric settlement so far discovered in Southeast Asia, with early evidence of farming and bronze-making.

reviewer_note: Coordinates converted from the DMS given by UNESCO (N17 24 27.979 E103 14 15.32). UNESCO says first discovered 1966; other pages say 1957, so discovery date is omitted. Penn says nearly 4,000 years ago, UNESCO 1495 BC; kept UNESCO range.
